title: Mini probe playbook and SLI synthesis for tokenized inference
content:
Goal: give oncall + product a tiny, repeatable set of probes + metric names + trace annotations so we can run a 2-week pilot across console, serving-runtime, private-deployments.

High level problems we want to catch early (fast feedback):
- sudden increase in TTF (time-to-first-token) for interactive calls
- multi-model fanout causing tail latency regressions
- tenant-specific cost spikes from repeated cold-kv misses
- silent quality regressions that correlate with quantization/variant rollouts

Quick experiments (probes) - aim to be cheap and actionable:
1) client-ttf-synthetic (client-side)
   - lightweight synthetic that mimics common user prompt (50-120 tokens)
   - emit as probe with tags: probe=client-ttf, env, tenant, route_policy
   - sample 1% of production users; instrument SDK to log client.start_ts and client.first_token_ts
   - target: detect 2x median increase over baseline in 30m window

2) model-fanout-heat-probe (server-side)
   - trigger multi-model path that causes cached vs uncached flows (A/B like)
   - annotate traces with: model.name, model.variant, kv.cache_hit (true/false), route_policy, token_count
   - capture full-span latency at 50/95/99 quantiles and top N callsites

3) kv-warmth-probe (tenant-weighted)
   - per-tenant mini-probe that simulates repeated low-variance sequences to exercise KV lookup patterns
   - metric: kv.cache_hit_rate_window_5m, kv.evictions_per_min, kv.prefetch_miss_rate
   - priority: apply to top 20% tenant by RPS first

Metric naming conventions (quick rules — keep short, machine-friendly):
- obs.metric.<component>.<signal>.<unit> where possible
  e.g., obs.metric.serving.ttl.first_token_ms, obs.metric.kv.cache_hit_rate.pct
- Span annotations (trace labels): model.name, model.variant, route_policy, tenant.id (hashed), prompt.hash (optional)
- Avoid free-text prompt content in traces — use prompt.hash or signature to allow replay without PII

Dashboard tile guidance (micro-kit):
- Tile A: TTF heatmap (by tenant cohort) — x-axis time, y-axis tenant-pctile, color by median cost-per-token
- Tile B: Fanout-latency breakdown — stacked bars for kernel/dispatch/kv/compile-time per quantile
- Tile C: KV Warmth tracker — rolling 5m cache_hit_rate by tenant, with eviction overlay
- Tile D: Probe healthboard — pass/fail counter, last-failure-trace link, owner

Sampling & trace budget notes:
- Adaptive sampling: sample every trace that fails a revival SLI (e.g., TTF > threshold), plus 0.5% baseline for normal traces
- For high cardinality tenants, downsample trace annotations but keep metric counters at full fidelity
- PII: apply redaction at SDK edge. If tenant identifiers needed, use HMAC-shared-salt hashing.

SLI synthesis (2-layers):
- User-facing SLIs (prod-facing): ttf_p50_ms, ttf_p95_ms, gen_completion_success_rate (percentage non-error), cost_per_1000_tokens_usd
- Service SLIs (infrastructure ops): kv_cache_hit_rate_<pool>, model_variant_error_rate, dispatch_queue_time_p95_ms
- Alerting heuristics: combine small relative shifts with absolute thresholds to avoid alert fatigue (e.g., alert when ttf_p95 increases >30% AND exceeds 400ms)

Investigation-first runbook (15-min triage flow):
- Step 0: consult Probe healthboard — did a probe fail? which tenants affected?
- Step 1: check TTF heatmap and fanout breakdown for sudden quantile shifts
- Step 2: follow trace anchors (span id) from failed probe — look for kv.cache_hit=false spikes, long kernel compile spans, or routing fallbacks
- Step 3: check rollout flags (FeatureFlag: model_variant) + recent deploys (link to GH PR in linked_artifacts)
- Step 4: if tenant-specific, trigger tenant isolation (route to dedicated variant) and open JIRA with annotated traces

Integration checklist (pilot):
- [ ] SDK: emit client.start_ts, client.first_token_ts, partition keys; redaction for PII
- [ ] Runtime: add standard span annotations (model.name, model.variant, kv.cache_hit) across model-serving codepaths
- [ ] Dashboards: create the 4 tiles above in a shared dashboard; add probe healthboard and oncall bookmark
- [ ] Alerts: implement compound alert for TTF spike + kv eviction surge; set initial sensitivity conservative
- [ ] Owner: assign owners per tile (serving-runtime, console, private-deployments)

Open questions / discussion points (notes-to-self):
- What sampling multiplier do we give interactive sessions vs batch? (idea: interactive x2)
- Should cost-per-token be a derived metric or stored raw? where to keep provenance?
- How to instrument third-party model variants that run in partner infra? need a shim for span annotation

Short-term action items (next 2 weeks):
- Priya: draft minimal SDK patch for client ttf emission (JIRA-OBS-1010)
- Ethan: add trace annotation middleware in serving runtime and wire kv.cache_hit flag (PR #27)
- Marina: spin up pilot dashboard and tag owners; invite SRE oncall to beta view
- Daniel: prototype adaptive sampling rule with retention tiers for traces

Slack threads / refs: slack:#obs-probes (discussion), confluence:CONFLUENCE-OBS-1123 (pilot charter)

Notes: keep this intentionally short. We expect lots of iteration; keep probes tiny and easy to roll back. This is a low ceremony, high-velocity experiment to reduce mean time to detect and mean time to mitigation for tokenized inference regressions.
